uncited: They explain why static load balancing schemes fail to achieve uniform execution times across processors.
The method does not compute a single scalar value but categorizes the sources of variance in processor execution time.
**Subvolume size: number of elements**: The count of unstructured grid elements (e.g., tetrahedra, hexahedra) assigned to a processor.
**Subvolume size: physical size (projected area)**: The 2D projected area of the subvolume on the image plane.
**Opacity transfer functions**: The mapping from scalar data values to opacity.
Transfer functions that result in higher average opacity cause rays to terminate earlier (shorter ray segments), while transparent regions require longer ray traversal.
**Viewing angle**: The orientation of the camera relative to the unstructured grid.
**Zoom in/out**: The magnification level of the view.
Zooming changes the resolution of the image plane relative to the world coordinates, affecting the number of rays cast and the precision of intersection calculations.
The factors are qualitative descriptors of workload variance rather than a computational algorithm.
They are observed through timing analysis of parallel execution.
